name: Song (state)
alt: Song of the Spring and Autumn period

predecessors.name: Shang dynasty
predecessors.text: the Shang heartland around Shangqiu, enfeoffed to a member of the defeated Shang royal house

successors.name: Qi (state)
successors.text: Song annexed by Qi in 286, 'with troops from Chu and Wei serving on behalf of Qi'

successors.name: Chu
successors.text: Chu's share of the partition 'by Qi, Chu and Wei' (King Kang page)

successors.name: Wei (Warring States)
successors.text: Wei's share of the partition 'by Qi, Chu and Wei'; King Kang fled to Wei

ledger.x: 1046: the Zhou enfeoff the Shang royal house at Shangqiu and the state of Song begins.
480: Cliopatria adds 24 cells of Lu's western edge to Song.
450: Cliopatria adds 20 cells of its Xu row to Song.
404: Cliopatria passes one cell of Lu to Song.
404: Cliopatria passes one cell of Song to Qi.
366: Cliopatria adds 3 cells from Zheng's last shape.
328: Dai Yan kills Lord Ticheng, takes the throne and styles himself King Kang of Song; the ducal house of Zi gives way to the Dai.
297: King Kang of Song annihilates Teng.
286: Qi, with Chu and Wei, destroys Song and the land is partitioned.

wars.name: Song's war with Chu and the Battle of the Hong River
wars.outcome: 'The Song forces were defeated at the battle of Hong in 638'; Duke Xiang's reign ends in 637 on the page's list.

wars.name: Jin-Chu campaign for Song and Cao (Chengpu)
wars.outcome: 'After Jin defeated Chu at the Battle of Chengpu in 632 BC, Jin crushed the State of Cao, rescued the State of Song'; Song's border was unchanged.

wars.name: Song's annexation of Cao
wars.outcome: Duke Jing of Song attacked Cao; Cao was exterminated in 487 and Jin sent no troops to rescue it.

wars.name: Song's annihilation of Teng
wars.outcome: Teng, a vassal of Lu and nominally conquered by Yue in 414, was annihilated by King Kang of Song.

wars.name: Qi, Chu and Wei conquest of Song
wars.outcome: King Min of Qi 'plotted with the states of Chu and Wei for a joint expedition against Song'; Song was partitioned by Qi, Chu and Wei; King Kang fled to Wei.

certainty.note: The ancient frontiers of the Song plain are drawn from city territories (Dingtao, Tengzhou, Shangqiu); no treaty or survey lines exist.
